verdict: pass (0 blocking, 0 technical defect in the guard/sampler behaviour, 8 observations)

observations.summary: delivery dry-run's increment case aborts on the free-floor rule, so it does not actually exercise the increment>=3072 rule
observations.detail: logs/inject-delta.log ends with guard_stop reason=free_below_floor free_mib=8640 (the injected used=7400 implies free=8640 < 10240, and the free check runs before the increment check). Expect-Abort only asserts that some GUARD_ABORT happened. The README table presents the case as proof of the increment rule.
observations.severity: observation (test-quality issue in the delivered dry-run; the guard rule itself is correct and QA covered it: 3071 pass, 3072 abort, half-rule total=4000 => 2000 abort)
observations.suggested_action: increment case should keep free >= 10240 in the injected snapshot (free/used are independent inputs) and assert the abort reason, not just the fact of an abort

observations.summary: sampler stats in README/receipt do not match the committed samples.csv and sampler log
observations.detail: README section 3 and receipt.dryrun.sampler say 4199/11863/41; committed logs/samples.csv and logs/sampler-dryrun.log say 4200/11862/39. The dry-run writes into the committed evidence logs by default, so a later run can silently overwrite raw logs while the narrative keeps older numbers.
observations.suggested_action: re-run with -EvidenceDir under target/ and update the narrative, or state that the numbers describe a specific run

observations.detail: a clean dry-run re-execution prints 18 PASS lines (3 parser + 10 sampler + 5 injection) and 0 FAIL; README/receipt say 20 checks.

observations.summary: Resolve-GuardPwsh toolchain fallback claim does not hold in the shells actually used
observations.detail: under Windows PowerShell 5.1 (pwsh not on PATH, target/toolchains/powershell-7.6.7/bin/pwsh.exe exists) Resolve-GuardPwsh returns 'powershell.exe', not the toolchain pwsh. Under pwsh 7.6.7 the fallback resolves only when the caller script's grandparent happens to be the repo root (e.g. caller at <repo>\target\qa-guard); for a caller under <repo>\scripts the double Split-Path yields the repo's parent, so the toolchain scan misses too. Practical impact: none observed - the loop is PS 5.1 compatible and produced 13 samples in both shells - but the README/receipt wording overstates the resolver.
observations.suggested_action: resolve the repo root from the template file path ($PSScriptRoot of the template script, or a parameter) and test both shells; or relax the documentation

observations.summary: empty injected Apps logs contexts=1 (bogus null pid)
observations.detail: Assert-Guard assigns $apps = if (...) { @() } else {...}; an empty array branch becomes $null, and $null | ForEach-Object { $_.pid } runs once with $_ = $null, so $pids = @($null) and the log says contexts=1. Abort decisions are unaffected (a $null baseline pid is skipped), but injection/dry-run logs show a misleading context count.
observations.suggested_action: use @($apps) with an explicit empty-array branch or guard with if ($apps) { ... } else { @() }

observations.summary: empty nvidia-smi line raises a parameter-binding error instead of GUARD_ABORT
observations.detail: ConvertFrom-GpuCsvLine has [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Line; an empty string cannot bind, so the caller sees 'Cannot bind argument to parameter Line because it is an empty string' rather than GUARD_ABORT. Missing columns / non-numeric cells (the acceptance cases) do raise GUARD_ABORT correctly.
observations.severity: observation (edge case; no empty-line observation on this machine)

observations.summary: capture-phase local-override trigger record is described without a path/line citation
